title: Kentucky Days and the kid band that won over a military band
summary: At Biloxi, soldiers joke about a kindergarten band, then applaud Laine's boys' playing of Kentucky Days.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah. You remember that one? That's old. Oh, yeah. Tell him I found a record of Kentucky Days yesterday. He found a record of Kentucky Days yesterday. Oh. Yeah.

That was my favorite. Is that right? I'll tell you a little instance that's happened about Kentucky Days. Now, this is a queer thing with our boy, Alfred. I've got three bands in Biloxi. Understand me? Uh-huh. I've got a band for West End Junior, band for West End Fire Company, number three, and a band for volunteer, number one. Okay. It was a park right on the other side of Kennedy's Hotel. Great big park. And there was a military band in this park. And there was a park. And there was a park. And they were sitting all around the mound. And they were talking. And they seen all my kids, a bunch of my kids out. All little fellas. Like the Georgie Brunas, Henny Brunas, and all that bunch. Kids, my boy, you know. Young, young kids. And they seen them walking around, you understand. And they had the uniforms on, see. So, uh, one fella in that bunch of soldier band, military band, he passed a remark. He said, Jesus, look at this. This must be a kindergarten band. I'd like to hear them play. He'd like to hear them play. Well, now that was carried over to me. I was right across the street from the park. See. So, all right. They, uh, they all got together, were ready to leave. To go on a parade. And they struck up any bones, any bottles today.

You understand? Uh-huh. I got all the kids together. Play Kentucky Days. When you come to that trill, come down soft. Be sure you do that. They were listening to me, you know. All right. They got around there and they popped them loose. First damn thing you know, them soldiers, when they finished, they took their hats off. Like that was doing that, waving at that kid band. Waving at that kid band. That was the kindergarten band they were going to hear. That's good.
